title: Creating, Saving, Copying, and Organizing Files and Folders
path: Creating, Saving, Copying, and Organizing Files and Folders

headings.title: Introduction to Digital File Management
headings.content: Digital file management is the structured practice of storing, naming, and organizing electronic documents on a computer system. For a midwife working in a modern Nigerian health facility, this skill is just as vital as keeping clean physical case notes. A **file** is an individual container of data, such as an antenatal clinic roster saved as a spreadsheet or a referral letter typed as a document. A **folder** is a digital directory used to group related files together, preventing your desktop from becoming cluttered with loose items. Understanding how these elements interact forms the foundation of safe and efficient health record keeping.

headings.title: Creating New Files and Folders
headings.content:
To start storing digital information, you must first know how to create new containers. 

1. **Creating a Folder**: Navigate to the location where you want the folder to live, right-click on an empty space, select 'New', and then choose 'Folder'. Type a clear name immediately while the text is highlighted.
2. **Creating a File**: Open the specific application you need—such as a word processor or spreadsheet program—and begin your work. When you choose to initiate a new blank document, the application generates a temporary file ready for your data.

Always name your creations immediately using descriptive titles rather than leaving them as 'New Folder' or 'Document 1'.

headings.title: Saving Files and Folders
headings.content: Creating a document is only the first step; saving ensures your work is written permanently to the computer's storage drive. When you use the **Save As** command, you choose both the destination folder and the file name. This differs from a simple **Save**, which merely updates an already existing file with your latest changes. A common mistake among beginners is typing long documents without saving periodically, risking total data loss if a sudden power outage occurs—a frequent challenge in many Nigerian workplaces. Cultivate the habit of saving your work every few minutes.

headings.title: Copying, Moving, and Deleting Items
headings.content:
Managing your files often requires rearranging them or creating duplicates for backup purposes.

- **Copying**: Creates an exact duplicate of a file or folder in a new location while leaving the original intact.
- **Moving**: Relocates the item from its current folder to a completely new destination without leaving a copy behind.
- **Deleting**: Sends unwanted items to the Recycle Bin or Trash, freeing up storage space. 

Be careful when deleting files that contain sensitive clinical audits or patient rosters, ensuring you truly no longer need them before clearing your trash folder.

headings.title: Structuring and Organizing Directories
headings.content: An organized computer directory functions much like a well-run antenatal clinic archive. Instead of dropping every document into a single main folder, create a hierarchical structure. For example, make a main folder named 'Maternity_Unit', and inside it, create subfolders for 'Antenatal', 'Labour_Ward', and 'Immunization_Records'. Within those subfolders, you might further separate files by month or year. This logical grouping ensures that when a supervisor asks for last quarter's immunization tally, you can locate it in seconds rather than hunting blindly across the entire hard drive.

headings.title: Best Practices for Maintaining a Clean Directory
headings.content: Maintaining a pristine digital workspace requires consistent habits. Adopt clear naming conventions that include dates, such as '2023_Antenatal_Report_Final', so files sort chronologically. Avoid using overly long or cryptic abbreviations that only make sense to you on the day you type them. Regularly back up important health records to an external hard drive or secure cloud storage to protect against hardware failure. Finally, schedule a monthly clean-up session to archive old documents and empty your trash bin.
